newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares dip on profit-taking, prospects good.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares dip on profit-taking, prospects good.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on profit-taking on Tuesday with the outlook good after Wall Street rose on Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's generally upbeat assessment of the U.S. economy at a Senate hearing.
"Bonds and shares will be affected by Greenspan's remarks tomorrow, but the outlook is optimistic after the Dow Jones rose in mid-morning trade," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index lost 1.61 point to 142.75 in overall bourse turnover of 1.393 billion crowns. The KFX March future fell 1.25 point to 143.50 with 70 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

Banks and A.P. Moeller took the brunt of the fall. Den Danske Bank dropped five crowns to close at 487, rival Unidanmark shed 11 crowns to 340, while D/S 1912 and D/S Svendborg lost 5,000 and 3,000 crowns respectively to close at 174,000 and 252,000.
Bucking the downward trend were Tele Danmark, the day's most traded paper, which closed one crown up at 337 and Copenhagen Airports, which ended 4.7 crowns higher at 685.
